claim: In 2024, oil flow through the Strait of Hormuz averaged 20 million barrels a day, about 20% (one in five) of global petroleum liquids consumption.

evidence.quote: In 2024, oil flow through the strait averaged 20 million barrels per day (b/d), or the equivalent of about 20% of global petroleum liquids consumption.
about one-fifth of global oil and petroleum product consumption

notes: Dated 2024. Say 'In 2024', never present tense: UNCTAD (1 Apr 2026) says traffic collapsed after 28 Feb 2026 (C009).

claim: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Oman and Iran and connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea.

evidence.quote: located between Oman and Iran, connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea

notes: Use EIA's names. Show no borders as the subject; label only the strait and the two countries.

claim: EIA: very few alternative options exist to move oil out of the Gulf if the strait is closed.

evidence.quote: very few alternative options exist to move oil out of the strait if it is closed

notes: EIA adds that some pipelines can bypass it (C008).

claim: EIA estimates 84% of the crude oil and condensate that moved through Hormuz in 2024 went to Asian markets.

evidence.quote: 84% of the crude oil and condensate and 83% of the liquefied natural gas that moved through the Strait of Hormuz went to Asian markets in 2024

notes: An EIA estimate. The brief's '89%' is not in EIA's pages (myths M2).

claim: China, India, Japan and South Korea were the top destinations for Hormuz crude moving to Asia in 2024, a combined 69% of all Hormuz crude and condensate flows.

evidence.quote: China, India, Japan, and South Korea were the top destinations for crude oil moving through the Strait of Hormuz to Asia, accounting for a combined 69% of all Hormuz crude oil and condensate flows in 2024

notes: The brief's '74%' is not in EIA's pages (myths M2). The script names the four countries and does not say 69%.

claim: In 2024 the US imported about 0.5 million b/d of crude and condensate from Persian Gulf countries through Hormuz: about 7% of its crude imports and 2% of its petroleum liquids consumption.

evidence.quote: accounting for about 7% of total U.S. crude oil and condensate imports and 2% of U.S. petroleum liquids consumption

notes: '2% of consumption' is for imports via Hormuz only; prices are global, so say 'direct supply', not 'unaffected'.

claim: EIA says Asian markets (China, India, Japan, South Korea) would likely be the most affected by supply disruptions at Hormuz.

evidence.quote: These markets would likely be most affected by supply disruptions at Hormuz.

notes: EIA's judgement ('would likely'), so the script credits EIA.

claim: EIA estimates about 2.6 million b/d of Saudi and UAE pipeline capacity could bypass Hormuz in a disruption, roughly an eighth of the 20 million b/d that flows through.

evidence.quote: about 2.6 million b/d of capacity from the Saudi and UAE pipelines could be available to bypass the Strait of Hormuz in the event of a supply disruption

notes: Not in the script (the Short already carries three numbers). A pinned-comment fact.

claim: UNCTAD (1 April 2026): after an escalation on 28 February 2026, ship transits through Hormuz fell from about 130 a day in February to 6 in March, a drop of about 95%, and the strait remained virtually closed.

evidence.locator: 'A critical supply route at a standstill'
evidence.quote: Ship transits dropped from around 130 per day in February to just 6 in March - a collapse of about 95%.
The Strait of Hormuz remains virtually closed

notes: A dated 2026 observation by a UN body, not today's status. Not in the script; AK decides whether a 2026 beat is wanted (open_questions 1).

claim: EIA calls the Strait of Hormuz one of the world's most important oil chokepoints, and defines chokepoints as narrow channels along widely used sea routes.

evidence.quote: it is one of the world's most important oil chokepoints
Chokepoints are narrow channels along widely used global sea routes that are critical to global energy security.

notes: Supports the word 'narrow' in the hook. EIA gives no width; the Short shows no measurement.
